what_its_for: Macitentan is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the arteries that carry blood to your lungs. It helps relax and widen these blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard, which can help you breathe more easily and do more physical activities.
how_to_take: Swallow one tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet.
dosing: The usual dose is one 10 mg tablet taken by mouth once daily. Do not change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store macitentan at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep this medicine in its original packaging and out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Do not get pregnant while taking this medicine — it can cause serious birth defects or loss of the pregnancy. Women who can get pregnant must use two reliable forms of birth control during treatment and for at least one month after stopping. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit as it may increase the amount of this drug in your body. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, especially rifampin (an antibiotic), ketoconazole or fluconazole (antifungals), or HIV medicines, as these can interact with macitentan.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice any of the following: signs of liver problems such as nausea, stomach pain, yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, or dark urine; signs of low red blood cell count (anemia) such as unusual tiredness, pale skin, or shortness of breath; swelling of your hands, feet, or legs; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; or if you think you may be pregnant.
when_it_works: Macitentan starts working right away in your body, but you may not notice improvements in your symptoms for several weeks to months. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel the same, because it is working to slow the progression of your disease. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: This drug must NOT be used during pregnancy. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting, every month during treatment, and one month after stopping. You must be enrolled in a special safety program called the Opsumit REMS Program to receive this medicine. LIVER DISEASE: This medicine is not recommended if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Your doctor will check your liver function before and during treatment. KIDNEY DISEASE: No dose adjustment is needed for kidney problems, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. ELDERLY: Older adults can take this medicine, but may need closer monitoring. CHILDREN: Safety and effectiveness have not been established in patients under 18 years of age.
